neighbours.label: the word stem react- (' reaction', ' reactive', ' reacts', ' reacted'), strongest in the chemical / physical sense; the + pole instead predicts an upcoming 'reaction'
fire: Heat is given off when the reaction between lime and water begins.
Fluorine is the most reactive of all the halogens.
Iron reacts slowly with damp air to form rust.
Enzymes lower the energy needed for a reaction to start.
In the flask the two gases reacted to form a white smoke.
A chain reaction in the reactor core is kept in check by control rods.
The rate of the reaction doubles with every ten degrees.
Potassium is so reactive that it is stored under oil.
quiet: Heat is given off when lime is stirred into water.
Fluorine is the lightest of all the halogens.
Iron rusts slowly in damp air and turns brown.
Enzymes lower the energy needed for digestion to start.
In the flask the two gases combined to form a white smoke.
The crowd's response to the speech was louder than expected.
The speed of the process doubles with every ten degrees.
Potassium is so soft that it can be cut with a knife.

notes: Card: ' reaction' x11, ' reactive' x6, ' Reactive' x3, ' reacts' x2 in chemistry / biochemistry text. Probes: chemical reaction 0.59/0.41, Reactive oxygen 0.66, reacts 0.64, 'reacted angrily' 0.48, 'reacted with joy' 0.32, emotional noun 'reaction' 0.13-0.27, allergic reaction 0.19, no react- word 0.05. So the word carries it and the chemical sense adds to it; the test's fire items are all chemical.
